meta.brandingNote: Labels only - change them for any course. badge is the little square top-left (an emoji or up to 4 characters). Drop course/courseName and the line under the name disappears. Add "subtitle" if you want a line under the big heading; leave it out and there is none. meta._: ---- the rest is documentation, not settings ----
readThisFirst: This file controls EVERYTHING the page loads. The page has no list of its own.
'sources' is resolved at load time and every result is merged into one random pool.
Turn any source off with "enabled": false instead of deleting it.
Click the chip at the top right of the page to see what each source returned, or why it failed.

sourceTypes.clips: an inline list, right here in this file
sourceTypes.folder: a folder of video files; read live when the page is served, otherwise from that source's 'manifest' list
sourceTypes.gdriveFolder: a shared Google Drive folder; needs a free Google API key, see the notes on that source
sourceTypes.json: another list file, local or on any https URL

srcTypes: Every clip needs exactly one 'src'. The player works out what it is.
Instagram   -> https://www.instagram.com/reel/CODE/          click to start, loops, no end signal
YouTube     -> https://youtu.be/ID  (Shorts too)             autoplays, plays once, reports the end
Vimeo       -> https://vimeo.com/123456789                   autoplays, plays once, reports the end
Direct file -> https://example.com/clip.mp4                  autoplays, plays once, reports the end
In the repo -> videos/clip.mp4                               autoplays, plays once, reports the end
Drive file  -> https://drive.google.com/file/d/ID/view       click to start, no end signal
Optional per clip: 'kind' forces a renderer, 'link' sets the arrow button, 'disabled': true parks it.
meta.note: Served over https from GitHub Pages. Every src must be a public link or a file committed inside this folder - a page on the web cannot read files on your PC.

sources.name: Video files in this repo
sources.note: Off, because the list is all links. If you ever commit video files into videos/, set enabled to true and put their filenames in 'manifest' (sync-clips.bat does that for you locally). A folder listing cannot be read on GitHub Pages, which is what 'manifest' is for.

sources.name: Shared Google Drive folder
sources.note: Off, and not needed while everything is links. To switch it on you need a free Google API key: console.cloud.google.com -> new project -> enable 'Google Drive API' -> Credentials -> API key -> paste it into apiKey above. Google refuses to list a folder to an anonymous caller, so there is no key-free way. The folder must stay shared as 'Anyone with the link'. Note the key sits in this file in a public repo, so restrict it to the Drive API and to your GitHub Pages domain.

sources.name: Extra list file
sources.note: Off. Point this at another clips file - a second list in the repo, or any https URL - and its clips join the same pool.
